children.name: Nyctibius
children.description: Solitary, nocturnal insectivores with enormous gaping mouths and cryptic plumage that allows them to perch upright on a dead tree stump and resemble a broken branch. Their large yellow eyes close to tiny slits during the day, completing the camouflage.

children.name: Nyctibius griseus
children.description: The common potoo, or kakuy (Nyctibius griseus), or urutau is one of seven species of birds within the genus Nyctibius.

children.name: Nyctibius grandis
children.description: The great potoo or grand potoo (Nyctibius grandis) is the largest potoo species and is widely distributed in Central and South America.

children.name: Nyctibius aethereus
children.description: The long-tailed potoo (Nyctibius aethereus) is a species of bird in the family Nyctibiidae. It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

children.name: Nyctibius jamaicensis
children.description: The northern potoo (Nyctibius jamaicensis) is a nocturnal bird belonging to the potoo family, Nyctibiidae. It is found from Mexico south to Costa Rica, and on the islands of Jamaica and Hispaniola (in the Dominican Republic and Haiti). It was formerly classified as a subspecies of the common potoo (Nyctibius griseus) but is now usually treated as a separate species based on differences in vocalizations.

children.name: Nyctibius leucopterus
children.description: The white-winged potoo (Nyctibius leucopterus) is a species of bird in the family Nyctibiidae. It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

children.name: Nyctibius bracteatus
children.description: The rufous potoo (Phyllaemulor bracteatus) is a species of bird in the family Nyctibiidae.

children.name: Nyctibius maculosus
children.description: The Andean potoo (Nyctibius maculosus) is a species of bird in the family Nyctibiidae.
